quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: You must always let pedestrians cross first if they are in or entering a crosswalk. Pay attention to pedestrians when you drive through intersections or turn.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires are the best choice for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other bad conditions. Winter is hard for drivers and requires extra care. Always check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter. Snow tires help your vehicle grip slippery roads better.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." This means:

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should go 35 mph only when the weather is bad.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell drivers to slow down. The new speed limit shown on the sign begins right at that sign.

questions.question: Always use your turn signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Entering or leaving a parking space.
Entering traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal for any move to the left or right. Signal when you enter traffic from a parking space, move into a new lane, or pass another vehicle.

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up and pull in front of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: When passing a bicycle, slow down and give as much space as you can. Bicycles have less protection than cars. Passing too fast can make the bicyclist lose control.

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Have large blind spots.
Can stop faster than passenger vehicles.
Do not need more room to turn than passenger vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Stay away from these areas. Because trucks are big and heavy, they need more space to turn and stop than regular cars.

questions.question: A fire engine is following you on a two-lane street without using emergency lights or sirens. You should:

options.text: Drive normally.
Stop as fast as you can.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down, move right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive normally.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is following you without its siren or lights on, you do not need to pull over. Drive normally.

questions.question: Before turning left, you must:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Let oncoming vehicles pass first.
Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait for oncoming traffic to get a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let oncoming vehicles pass first.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic signal, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go first.

questions.question: Two solid yellow lines mean:

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is not allowed.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic is moving toward you on the other side. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: On a narrow road meeting an oncoming vehicle, you must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
Tell the other vehicle to pull over.
Turn on your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, both drivers must share the road equally. Each vehicle needs enough space to pass safely.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are crossing.
Keep driving. You have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the intersection is dangerous. Always treat it like a stop sign and come to a complete stop.

questions.question: How should you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, let other traffic go first, and match the speed of traffic already on the freeway.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check the traffic.
Always stop completely before entering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, let other traffic go first, and match the speed of traffic already on the freeway.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway, signal and match the speed of traffic. Always yield to cars already on the freeway.

questions.question: You are in traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates. What should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way. You do not need to check for trains.
You can pass slower drivers while crossing.
Make sure your vehicle can cross all the way without stopping.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross all the way without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before crossing railroad tracks, make sure you have enough space to get completely across without stopping. Never pass other vehicles at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing.

questions.question: Your body removes about how much alcohol per hour?

options.text: Three drinks per hour.
One drink per hour.
Two drinks per hour.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: One drink per hour.
questions.explanation: Most people's bodies process about one drink in one hour. How impaired you become depends on how much you drink, how fast you drink it, your weight, what you eat, and your health.

questions.question: Your wheels drop off the road onto the shoulder. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car at the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: If your wheels go off the pavement, slow down without braking hard. Carefully steer back onto the road. Watch for other traffic when returning to the road.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, along with fog lights if you have them. High beams bounce off fog and reduce visibility.

questions.question: Which is a sign of a drunk driver?

options.text: Weaving between lanes.
Driving slower than normal traffic.
Making sudden stops.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving too slowly, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another car is coming toward you. Your headlights should be on:

options.text: High beam.
Low beam.
Off, with parking lights only.
Either high or low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam.
questions.explanation: Always use low beam headlights when another car is approaching or if you are following another car at night. This keeps everyone safe.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. How should you merge into traffic?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Use the ramp to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Let traffic on the freeway go first.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use the ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic and yield to cars already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots to find a safe gap before merging.

questions.question: What does this road sign show?

options.text: The safe speed limit for a residential area.
The safe speed for leaving a highway.
The safe speed for entering a highway.
The safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The safe speed for leaving a highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the recommended speed for exiting a highway. In this example, it shows 30 mph.
